name: Toi
overview: The Scriptures identify Toi, also called Tou, as the king of Hamath who recognized the military victories of King David over Hadadezer. Upon hearing of David's triumph, Toi sent his son—named Joram or Hadoram—to greet and bless David, acknowledging the conflict between Toi and Hadadezer. This diplomatic gesture, accompanied by gifts of gold, silver, and brass vessels, highlights the respect and peace extended toward David following his conquest.
